examples.en: My house is a short distance from school.
I walk for short-distance trips.

examples.ko: 이 앱은 근거리에 있는 가게를 보여 줘요.
examples.en: This app shows stores that are nearby.
Short-distance buses have cheap fares.
The office is close, so I get there quickly.
I sent the photo through short-range communication.

explain: 반대말은 '원거리'예요. 가까운 곳에 갈 때는 '가까운 거리'라고 더 많이 말하고, '근거리'는 '근거리 통신', '근거리 이동'처럼 설명이나 안내문에서 자주 보여요.
explain_en: The opposite is 원거리 (long distance). In everyday speech people say 가까운 거리 more often; 근거리 shows up in fixed terms like 근거리 통신 (short-range communication) and in notices or explanations.

examples.en: The child lay flat on the floor.
The box got squashed flat when I stepped on it.
The cat pressed its ears flat.
I press the dough flat and bake it.
The balloon burst and shriveled up flat.
The bread sank flat, so it doesn't taste good.

explain: '납작'은 눌려서 넓고 얇아진 모양을 흉내 내는 말이에요. 형용사 '납작하다'와 함께 쓰이고, '납작 엎드리다'처럼 몸을 낮출 때 자주 나와요. '넓적하다'는 넓고 평평한 모양이고, '납작'은 눌려서 얇아진 느낌이 더 있어요.

phrases.example: 사장님이 화를 내자 직원들이 모두 납작 엎드렸어요.
phrases.en: keep one's head down; lie low
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸을 바닥에 낮춘다는 뜻에서 나와, 무서워서 눈치를 보며 조용히 숨죽이는 모습도 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: From pressing the body flat, it also describes keeping a low profile out of fear or deference.

explain_en: 납작 imitates the look of something pressed wide and thin. It pairs with the adjective 납작하다 and often appears in 납작 엎드리다 (to lie flat). 넓적하다 means broad and flat, while 납작 adds a feel of being pressed thin.

examples.en: My heart pounded before the presentation.
I trembled with a racing heart waiting for the results.
It was my first date, so my heart fluttered.
I was nervous with a pounding heart before opening the letter.

examples.ko: 놀이기구를 타기 전부터 심장이 두근두근 뛰어요.
examples.en: My heart starts thumping even before I get on the ride.
I opened the gift with excited anticipation.

explain: 설레거나 긴장할 때 심장이 뛰는 소리와 느낌을 흉내 내는 말이에요. 좋은 기대와 불안 둘 다에 쓰고, '두근거리다'와 '두근두근하다'는 같은 느낌의 동사예요. '쿵쾅쿵쾅'은 더 세게 뛸 때 써요.
explain_en: It imitates the sound and feeling of a heartbeat when you are excited or nervous, and works for both happy anticipation and anxiety. 두근거리다 and 두근두근하다 are verbs with the same feel. 쿵쾅쿵쾅 is for a much harder pounding.

examples.en: My heart always pounds before an interview.
My heart raced the night before the trip.

examples.ko: 그 사람을 보면 두근두근하는 마음을 숨길 수 없어요.
examples.en: I can't hide how my heart pounds when I see him.

examples.ko: 내일 결과를 기다릴 때도 가슴이 두근두근할 거예요.
examples.en: My heart will be pounding tomorrow too while I wait for the results.
My heart was pounding and my hands got sweaty.
My heart is racing, so I can't sleep.

explain: '가슴이 두근두근하다'처럼 주어는 보통 '가슴'이나 '마음'이에요. '두근거리다'도 같은 뜻으로 써요. 설렘과 긴장 둘 다 되지만, 무서워서 뛸 때는 '쿵쾅거리다'나 '떨리다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: The subject is usually 가슴 (chest) or 마음 (heart), as in 가슴이 두근두근하다. 두근거리다 means the same. It covers both excitement and nerves; for fear, 쿵쾅거리다 or 떨리다 sounds more natural.

examples.ko: 이 수업은 멀티미디어 자료를 많이 써요.
examples.en: This class uses a lot of multimedia material.
The multimedia classroom has a big screen.
That company makes multimedia content.
Multimedia devices are very diverse these days.
I majored in multimedia at university.
I'm going to see a multimedia exhibition.

explain: 영상, 소리, 글을 함께 쓴 자료나 기술을 말해요. 일상 대화보다는 수업, 광고, 직업 이름 앞에서 '멀티미디어 교실', '멀티미디어 콘텐츠'처럼 붙여 쓰는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It refers to materials or technology that combine video, sound, and text. It appears less in casual talk and more as a modifier in school, ads, and job contexts, such as 멀티미디어 교실 or 멀티미디어 콘텐츠.

examples.en: I know nothing about cooking.
Sorry, it's an uninformed question.

examples.ko: 그렇게 무식하게 힘으로만 하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't just use brute force like that.
My friend teased me, saying I'm clueless.
I was ignorant, so I didn't even know this.

examples.ko: 무식했던 저는 책을 많이 읽기 시작했어요.
examples.en: I used to be ignorant, so I started reading many books.

explain: 사람에게 직접 쓰면 '배우지 못한 사람'이라는 무례한 말이 될 수 있어서, 남에게 하지 않는 게 좋아요. 자기 자신에게 겸손하게 쓰거나 '무식하게 힘만 쓰다'처럼 방법이 투박하다는 뜻으로 많이 써요.
explain_en: Said directly to someone, it sounds rude, like calling them uneducated, so avoid using it about other people. Koreans use it humbly about themselves, or about a crude method, as in 무식하게 힘만 쓰다 (to rely on brute force).

examples.en: Einstein is a famous physicist.
My dream is to become a physicist.
Physicists discovered a new particle.

examples.ko: 그 물리학자는 우주에 대한 책을 썼어요.
examples.en: That physicist wrote a book about the universe.
My uncle is a physicist who works at a university.
The news interviewed a physicist.

explain: '과학자'가 넓은 이름이고, 물리학자·화학자·수학자는 분야별로 부르는 이름이에요. 대학 전공은 '물리학과'(또는 '물리 전공'), 연구하는 직업은 '물리학자'라고 구분해서 말해요. 소리, 빛, 힘, 에너지처럼 자연의 움직임을 다루는 사람에게 써요.
explain_en: 과학자 is the broad word, and 물리학자, 화학자, and 수학자 name the specific fields. A university major is 물리학과 (or 물리 전공), while the working scientist is a 물리학자. It is used for people who study motion, light, force, and energy.

examples.ko: 그렇게 혼자 다 하려는 건 미련해요.
examples.en: Trying to do it all alone like that is foolish.
It's a clumsy method, but it's sure.
Why am I so dense?
He just worked hard in a thickheaded way.
I think it's foolish to hold on while you're sick.
I was slow-witted and lost a lot.

explain: 머리가 나쁘다기보다 '요령 없이 고지식하다'는 느낌이 있어요. '곰처럼 미련하다'처럼 쓰고, '어리석다'보다 말이 거칠어요. 이름이 같은 명사 '미련'은 '아직 마음이 남아 있는 것'이라서 뜻이 달라요.
explain_en: It carries the sense of being rigid and lacking know-how rather than low intelligence, as in 곰처럼 미련하다. It is blunter than 어리석다. The noun 미련 sounds the same but means lingering attachment, so the meaning differs.

examples.en: My younger sibling has a lively personality.
She greeted me in a bright voice.

examples.ko: 그 옷을 입으니까 더 발랄해 보여요.
examples.en: You look more perky in that outfit.
The new employee laughed brightly.
The kid who used to be bubbly is quiet lately.
This song is upbeat, so it lifts my mood.

explain: 주로 젊은 사람의 밝고 생기 있는 분위기에 써요. 어른이나 나이 많은 분에게는 잘 안 써요. '명랑하다'는 성격이 밝다는 뜻이고, '발랄하다'는 통통 튀는 느낌이 더 있어요.
explain_en: It describes a bright, lively air, mostly for young people, and is rarely used for older adults. 명랑하다 means a cheerful personality, while 발랄하다 adds a bouncy, springy feel.

examples.en: I pinned a pretty badge on my bag.
I lost my school badge.
I got this badge at an event.
When you reach a goal in the app, you get a badge.

examples.ko: 재킷에 배지 몇 개를 모아서 붙였어요.
examples.en: I collected a few badges and stuck them on my jacket.
The teacher gave badges to outstanding students.

explain: 옷이나 가방에 다는 작은 장식이나 표시를 말해요. '뱃지'라고 쓰는 사람이 많지만 표준 표기는 '배지'예요. 앱이나 게임에서 보상으로 주는 아이콘도 같은 말로 불러요.
explain_en: It is a small pin or marker attached to clothes or a bag. Many people write it 뱃지, but the standard spelling is 배지. Reward icons in apps and games are called by the same word.

examples.en: I glued the broken cup with glue.
Glue got on my hand and won't come off.
I applied glue to the sole of the shoe.
The glue smell is too strong.
This glue sticks well to metal too.
Please keep the child from touching the glue.

explain: 한국에서는 강한 접착제를 두루 '본드'라고 불러요. 종이나 가벼운 것은 '풀'로 붙이고, 플라스틱·가죽·신발처럼 튼튼하게 붙여야 할 때 '본드'를 써요. 아주 빨리 붙는 것은 '순간접착제'라고 해서 구분해요.
explain_en: In Korea, 본드 is used for strong adhesive in general. Paper and light items are stuck with 풀 (paste); 본드 is for things that must hold firmly, like plastic, leather, or shoes. The very fast-bonding kind is called 순간접착제 (superglue), which is a separate word.

examples.en: The police patrol every night.
More neighborhood patrols made it safer.
I asked a patrolling police officer for directions.
I saw a patrol car in front of the school.
Security guards have set patrol times.

examples.ko: 공원에는 순찰 도는 사람이 없어서 불안해요.
examples.en: No one patrols the park, so I feel uneasy.

explain: '순찰을 돌다'가 가장 자주 쓰이는 짜임이에요. '순찰하다'는 같은 뜻의 동사인데, 문장에서는 '순찰을 돌다'가 더 자연스러울 때가 많아요. 경찰, 경비원, 군인이 주로 해요.
explain_en: The most common pattern is 순찰을 돌다. 순찰하다 means the same, but 순찰을 돌다 often sounds more natural in a sentence. Police, security guards, and soldiers are the usual patrollers.

examples.en: A police officer patrols the alley.
The security guard patrolled inside the building.

examples.ko: 밤에는 두 사람이 같이 순찰할 거예요.
examples.en: Two people will patrol together at night.
A patrolling car drove past.
We patrolled the coast and came back.
Volunteers patrol the neighborhood every night, so it is safe.

explain: '순찰하다'는 장소를 목적어로 받아서 '동네를 순찰하다'처럼 써요. '순찰을 돌다'도 많이 쓰고, 구경하며 걷는 '둘러보다'와는 달라서 경비나 단속 같은 임무가 있을 때 써요.
explain_en: 순찰하다 takes the place as its object, as in 동네를 순찰하다. 순찰을 돌다 is also common. Unlike 둘러보다 (look around), it implies a duty such as guarding or enforcement.

examples.en: I made a solution by putting salt in water.
This solution is blue.
In the experiment, I mixed the solution slowly.
The lens cleaning solution has run out.

examples.ko: 용액이 너무 진해서 물을 더 넣었어요.
examples.en: The solution was too concentrated, so I added more water.

examples.ko: 선생님이 두 가지 용액을 비교해 보라고 하셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher told us to compare two kinds of solutions.

explain: 어떤 물질이 물 같은 액체에 녹아 있는 것을 말해요. 과학 시간이나 실험에서 쓰고, 일상에서는 '액', '약', '세정액'처럼 구체적인 이름으로 부르는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It means a substance dissolved in a liquid such as water. You hear it in science classes and experiments; in daily life people usually use more concrete names such as 액, 약, or 세정액.

examples.en: The police held back the protesters.
The child ran into the road, so I stopped him quickly.
The staff stop people from taking photos.

examples.ko: 아무도 제지하는 사람이 없어서 싸움이 커졌어요.
examples.en: Nobody stopped them, so the fight got bigger.
I stepped in to stop the argument.
The guard will stop people from going in.

explain: '말리다'는 일상에서 가볍게 하지 말라고 할 때 쓰고, '제지하다'는 힘이나 권한으로 못 하게 막는 느낌이라 뉴스와 공식 글에서 자주 나와요. '막다'는 더 넓게 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: 말리다 is the everyday word for talking someone out of something. 제지하다 feels like stopping someone with force or authority, so it shows up often in news and formal writing. 막다 is the broader general word.

examples.en: The diameter of this circle is 10 centimeters.
I bought a pipe with a large diameter.
I measured the ball's diameter with a ruler.

examples.ko: 나사 직경이 맞지 않아서 안 들어가요.
examples.en: The screw diameter doesn't match, so it won't fit.
The pizza is 30 cm across, so it's enough for two.

examples.ko: 직경을 알면 원의 둘레도 구할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you know the diameter, you can also find the circle's circumference.

explain: 원이나 공의 가운데를 지나는 가장 긴 선의 길이예요. 같은 뜻으로 '지름'을 더 많이 쓰고, '직경'은 수학·공학 글에서 보여요. '반지름'은 직경의 반이에요.
explain_en: It is the length of the longest line through the center of a circle or sphere. 지름 is the more common word for the same thing, while 직경 appears in math and engineering. 반지름 is half of it.

examples.en: The child eats while dribbling soup.
The pants are long and drag on the floor.
Water is leaking out of the plastic bag.

examples.ko: 그 일을 질질 끌다가 결국 늦었어요.
examples.en: I dragged that task out and ended up late.
The puppy trails its leash around.
I watched the movie with tears streaming down.

explain: 액체가 계속 흐르거나 물건이 바닥에 끌릴 때 쓰는 흉내말이에요. 일을 빨리 끝내지 않고 시간을 끄는 것도 '질질 끌다'로 말해요.
explain_en: It imitates liquid dribbling steadily or something dragging along the ground. Putting off finishing something is also 질질 끌다.

examples.en: The economy stays sluggish for a long time.
Sales stagnated last year.
When the market slumps, stores have a hard time.
There is a plan to revive the stagnating area.

examples.ko: 분위기가 침체해서 아무도 말을 안 했어요.
examples.en: The mood was gloomy, so no one spoke.
I'm worried the economy will slump further.

explain: 경제, 시장, 분위기처럼 큰 것이 활기를 잃고 가라앉을 때 써요. 사람이 기운 없는 것에는 '우울하다', '처지다'가 더 자연스러워요. 뉴스에서는 '침체되다'도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is for big things such as the economy, a market, or the atmosphere losing energy and sinking. For a person feeling down, 우울하다 or 처지다 is more natural. In the news, 침체되다 is also widely used.

examples.en: I want to get a job at a public enterprise.
A public enterprise is a company owned by the state.
I'm preparing for the public enterprise exam.
They say pay at public enterprises is stable.
That public enterprise started a new business.
My older brother works at a public enterprise.

explain: 한국전력이나 한국철도공사처럼 나라나 지방 정부가 만든 회사예요. 반대말은 '사기업'이에요. 한국에서는 안정적이라서 취업 준비생에게 인기가 많아요.
explain_en: These are companies set up by the state or local government, like the national power or railway corporations. The opposite is 사기업 (private company). In Korea they are popular with job seekers for their stability.

examples.en: Public officials must be honest.
My father worked as a public servant for a long time.
The assets of public officials were disclosed.
The newly appointed official gave a greeting.
Public officials may not accept gifts.
I study to become a public official.

explain: 나라나 지방 정부 일을 하는 사람을 두루 가리켜요. 일상에서는 '공무원'이라고 더 많이 말하고, '공직자'는 뉴스나 법에서 윤리나 책임을 말할 때 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It covers anyone doing work for the national or local government. Everyday speech prefers 공무원, while 공직자 appears in the news and in law when talking about ethics and responsibility.

examples.en: The film received high praise from critics.
I felt great about the teacher's glowing praise.
Rave reviews poured in for this restaurant.
The boss's lavish praise gave me energy.
The new product earned rave reviews right after its launch.
The high praise is nice, but it's also pressure.

explain: '칭찬'보다 훨씬 강하게 최고라고 말하는 것이에요. 보통 '극찬을 받다', '극찬이 쏟아지다'로 쓰고, 뉴스나 리뷰에서 많이 나와요. 평범한 칭찬에는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: This is far stronger than 칭찬: it says something is the best. The usual patterns are 극찬을 받다 and 극찬이 쏟아지다, common in news and reviews. It isn't used for ordinary compliments.

examples.en: My friends rave about that restaurant.
A critic praised this book to the skies.
It's a show everyone raves about, so I went to see it.

examples.ko: 선생님이 제 발표를 극찬하실 줄 몰랐어요.
examples.en: I didn't expect my teacher to praise my presentation so highly.
Reporters are showering that player with praise.
Travelers rave about it, so my expectations are high.

explain: '칭찬하다'보다 훨씬 강해서 '최고다'라고 말하는 느낌이에요. 보통 사람이 아니라 영화, 음식, 공연, 선수 같은 대상을 말할 때 많이 써요. 가까운 사람에게 하는 가벼운 칭찬에는 어색해요.
explain_en: It is much stronger than 칭찬하다, as if saying something is the best. It is most often used for movies, food, performances, or athletes. It sounds odd for light compliments to someone close.

examples.en: The winner of the class president election was announced.
The winner thanked everyone.
The newly elected person starts work next month.
We did an interview with the winner.
They give prize money to the contest winner.
The winner's name appeared on the screen.

explain: 선거나 공모전에서 뽑힌 사람이에요. 선거에서는 '후보'가 이기면 '당선자'가 되고, 떨어지면 '낙선자'예요. 시험에 붙은 사람은 '합격자'라고 해서 달라요.
explain_en: This is someone chosen in an election or contest. In an election, a 후보 who wins becomes a 당선자; one who loses is a 낙선자. A person who passes an exam is a 합격자, which is a different word.

examples.en: I'm curious about this machine's mechanism.

examples.ko: 선생님이 병이 생기는 메커니즘을 설명해 주셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher explained the mechanism by which illness develops.
A watch runs on a precise mechanism.

examples.ko: 기억이 만들어지는 메커니즘은 아직 다 몰라요.
examples.en: We don't fully understand how memories form.
I'm studying how the market works.
This game has an interesting mechanic.

explain: 어떤 일이 어떤 원리와 순서로 일어나는지를 말해요. '구조'는 모양이 어떻게 이루어졌는지, '메커니즘'은 어떻게 작동하는지에 초점이 있어요. 영어 mechanism을 소리 나는 대로 쓴 말이라 설명하는 글에서 많이 나와요.
explain_en: It describes the principle and order in which something happens. 구조 focuses on how something is built, while 메커니즘 focuses on how it works. It is a loanword from English and mostly appears in explanatory writing.

examples.en: Students of our school use the library for free.
Branch students also take exams at the main campus.
The main campus is in Seoul.
The event is held in the main school auditorium.
Please make a reservation if you wish to visit our school.
My younger sibling moved from the main school to the branch.

explain: 분교나 지점이 있는 학교의 중심이 되는 학교를 말해요. 반대말은 '분교'예요. 학교 안내문에서 '우리 학교'를 격식 있게 말할 때도 '본교'를 써요.
explain_en: It is the central school when there are branch campuses; the opposite is 분교. School notices also use 본교 as a formal way to say 'our school'.

examples.en: The department head resigns next month.
He resigned last month for health reasons.

examples.ko: 사직하려면 한 달 전에 말해야 해요.
examples.en: To resign, you have to tell them a month ahead.
The team leader said he would resign, and everyone was surprised.
I wrote my reason for resigning in a letter.
I resigned, so I'm resting now.

explain: '그만두다'를 격식 있게 말한 것이에요. 회사 서류나 뉴스에서는 '사직서를 내다'가 자주 나오고, 친구끼리는 '회사 그만뒀어'라고 해요. 높은 자리에서 물러날 때는 '사임하다'를 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: This is a formal version of 그만두다. Documents and news say 사직서를 내다 (submit a resignation letter), while friends say 회사 그만뒀어. For leaving a high post, 사임하다 is sometimes used.

examples.en: Smile when the photo is taken.
The staff at that shop are always smiling.
I baked smiley-shaped cookies.

examples.ko: 아침에 거울 보고 스마일 연습을 해요.
examples.en: In the morning I practice smiling in the mirror.
I drew a smiley at the end of the letter.
The smile campaign brightened up the school.

explain: 영어 smile을 그대로 쓴 말이라 '웃음'이나 '미소'보다 가볍고 귀여운 느낌이에요. 광고, 캠페인, 사진 찍을 때, 이모티콘에서 자주 쓰고 일반 문장에서는 '웃다', '미소'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It is the English word smile used as is, so it feels lighter and cuter than 웃음 or 미소. You see it in ads, campaigns, photo moments, and emoticons; in ordinary sentences 웃다 or 미소 is more natural.

examples.en: I like drinks with carbonation.
The fizz is gone, so it tastes flat.
Fizzy drinks are bad for your teeth.
I drank sparkling water with lemon.
The carbonation is strong, so my throat stings.

examples.ko: 저는 탄산을 못 마셔서 물을 시켜요.
examples.en: I can't drink fizzy drinks, so I order water.

explain: 원래는 화학 용어지만 일상에서는 콜라나 사이다 속 '톡 쏘는 거품'을 '탄산'이라고 불러요. '탄산음료', '탄산수'처럼 붙여 쓰고, '탄산이 세다/약하다/빠지다'로 정도를 말해요.
explain_en: Originally a chemistry term, in daily life it means the fizz in cola or soda. It joins into words like 탄산음료 and 탄산수, and you describe strength with 탄산이 세다, 약하다, or 빠지다.

examples.en: Our team advanced to the tournament.
A tournament is where you're out if you lose.
The World Cup knockout stage has started.
I took part in a table tennis tournament.
I was surprised when I saw the tournament bracket.
The final tournament takes place on the weekend.

explain: 이긴 팀만 다음 경기로 올라가는 방식이에요. 모든 팀이 서로 한 번씩 겨루는 '리그'와 달라요. 보통 '토너먼트'만 말해도 이 방식의 대회를 가리키고, 대회 이름에 붙어서도 써요.
explain_en: This is a format where only the winners move on. It differs from a 리그 (league), where every team plays each other. Saying just 토너먼트 usually refers to this kind of event, and it also attaches to competition names.

examples.en: The school notifies parents of the results.
The company gave advance notice of the dismissal.
We will notify you of the changes by text message.

examples.ko: 통지하는 시기가 너무 늦어서 준비할 수 없었어요.
examples.en: The notice came too late for me to prepare.
They are notifying people of results by email.
The court notified us of the date, so I found out.

explain: 공식적으로 어떤 사실을 알려 줄 때 써요. 친구에게 알려 줄 때는 '알려 주다'가 자연스럽고, '통지하다'는 회사·학교·관공서 같은 곳이 정해진 방법으로 알릴 때 써요. 같은 말의 명사는 '통지', 서류는 '통지서'예요.
explain_en: It is for formally informing someone of a fact. To tell a friend, 알려 주다 is natural; 통지하다 is for institutions such as companies, schools, and offices notifying through set channels. The noun is 통지 and the document is 통지서.

examples.en: Residents evacuated because of the flood.
When the evacuation announcement plays, leave right away.
The evacuation site is the school playground.

examples.ko: 할머니는 전쟁 때 피난 이야기를 해 주셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother told me stories about fleeing during the war.
We do evacuation drills every year.
The evacuation was late, and many people suffered.

explain: 재난이나 전쟁 때 위험한 곳을 떠나 안전한 곳으로 가는 것이에요. '대피'는 지금 당장 몸을 피하는 느낌이고, '피난'은 집을 떠나 오래 머무는 경우까지 넓게 써요. '피난을 가다'로 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It means leaving a dangerous place for safety during a disaster or war. 대피 feels like getting out of harm's way right now, while 피난 extends to leaving home for a longer stay. The common pattern is 피난을 가다.

examples.en: Residents flee up the mountain.

examples.ko: 지진 때 우리 가족은 학교로 피난했어요.
examples.en: During the earthquake, my family took shelter at the school.

examples.ko: 태풍이 오면 높은 곳으로 피난할 거예요.
examples.en: If a typhoon comes, we will evacuate to higher ground.
The road was full of people fleeing.
A fire broke out, so we evacuated quickly and called.

examples.ko: 집이 물에 잠겨서 친척 집으로 피난해야 했어요.
examples.en: My house was flooded, so I had to take refuge at a relative's.

explain: 재난이나 전쟁에서 안전한 곳으로 가는 거예요. '대피하다'가 뉴스에서 더 자주 나오고, '피난하다'는 오래 떠나 있는 이야기에 어울려요. 몸만 피하는 '피하다'와는 달라서 장소로 옮겨 갈 때 써요.
explain_en: It means going to a safe place in a disaster or war. 대피하다 shows up more in the news, while 피난하다 suits stories of being away for longer. Unlike plain 피하다 (avoid), it implies moving to another location.

examples.en: The plane began its descent.
Mornings are cold because the temperature has dropped.

examples.ko: 엘리베이터 하강 속도가 빨라서 귀가 아팠어요.
examples.en: The elevator descended fast, and my ears hurt.
The plane shook because of a downdraft.
The stock price keeps falling.
I screamed the moment the roller coaster dropped.

explain: 위에서 아래로 내려가는 것을 격식 있게 말해요. 반대말은 '상승'이에요. 일상에서는 '내려가다', '떨어지다'를 많이 쓰고, '하강'은 비행기, 기온, 주가 같은 설명에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is the formal word for moving from up to down; the opposite is 상승. In daily life people say 내려가다 or 떨어지다, while 하강 appears in descriptions of planes, temperatures, and stock prices.

en: wear out; be tattered; become shabby

examples.en: The clothes wore out from long use.
The shoe soles wore through, so I bought new ones.

examples.ko: 이 가방은 자주 들면 모서리가 해져요.
examples.en: If you carry this bag often, the corners fray.
It's a shame to throw away worn socks.

examples.ko: 책 표지가 해지기 전에 커버를 씌웠어요.
examples.en: I put a cover on before the book jacket wore out.
I wore the jeans until the knees wore out.

explain: 옷, 신발, 가방처럼 오래 써서 닳고 찢어질 때 써요. '낡다'는 오래되어 허름해진 상태이고, '해지다'는 천이나 가죽이 닳아서 올이 풀리거나 구멍이 나는 변화예요. '해가 지다'와 소리는 비슷하지만 달라요.
explain_en: It is used when clothes, shoes, or bags wear down and fray from long use. 낡다 is the general state of being old and shabby, while 해지다 is the change of fabric or leather wearing thin or tearing. It sounds similar to 해가 지다 (the sun sets) but is unrelated.

examples.en: A hiker went missing in the mountains.

examples.ko: 태풍 때문에 어부 두 명이 행방불명됐대요.
examples.en: I heard two fishermen went missing because of the typhoon.
They are looking for the missing child.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 오 년 전에 행방불명됐다고 해요.
examples.en: They say he went missing five years ago.
If someone goes missing, you must contact the police right away.
The cat that left home is missing, and I'm worried.

explain: 사람이 어디 있는지 알 수 없게 된 상태예요. 물건이 안 보일 때는 쓰지 않고 '없어지다', '잃어버리다'를 써요. 뉴스에서는 '실종되다'도 같은 뜻으로 많이 나오는데, 이쪽이 더 짧고 흔해요.
explain_en: It describes a person whose whereabouts are unknown. For objects you don't use it; say 없어지다 or 잃어버리다. In the news 실종되다 is the same idea and is shorter and more common.

examples.en: The speed of the fall gets faster and faster.
We confirmed the falling of objects through an experiment.
The parachute drop training has started.
I filmed the ball dropping.
They hit the landing point exactly.
They put up a safety net to prevent falling accidents.

explain: 위에서 아래로 떨어지는 것을 과학이나 훈련 이야기에서 말해요. 일상에서는 '떨어지다'를 쓰고, '낙하'는 '낙하산', '자유 낙하', '낙하 사고'처럼 굳은 말에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is the dropping of something from above, used in science and training contexts. In daily speech people say 떨어지다; 낙하 appears in set terms such as 낙하산 (parachute), 자유 낙하, and 낙하 사고.

examples.en: Skin ages as you get older.
The doctor said my eyes aged early.
When cells age, the body weakens.
The speed of aging differs for each person.

examples.ko: 운동을 안 하면 몸이 더 빨리 노화할 거예요.
examples.en: If you don't exercise, your body will age faster.
You look aged in the face from heavy stress.

explain: 사람이나 몸의 기능이 나이 들어 약해지는 것을 과학적으로 말해요. 일상에서는 '늙다', '나이 들다'가 더 자연스러워요. 주어는 보통 '피부', '세포', '몸'처럼 몸이나 부분이에요.
explain_en: It describes the body or its functions weakening with age in a scientific tone. In daily speech 늙다 or 나이 들다 is more natural. The subject is usually the body or a part of it, such as skin or cells.
